exercise.name: Dumbbell Sumo Deadlift High Pull

reference.title: Dumbbell Sumo Deadlift High Pull (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Shoulders, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Compound (sumo deadlift, explosive hip extension, shrug and upright-row pull)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the bottom, breathe out as you pull, breathe in on the way down.

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbell; stop about 2-3 reps short of failure or when the hips slow
prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbell, more reps per round

cues.text: Wide stance, toes out, one dumbbell held vertically in both hands, hips down, chest up, arms long.
Drive the floor away, knees out, stand up fast.
Shrug and pull the dumbbell up the body, elbows high and out above the hands.
Hands at the upper chest, elbows high; do not lean back.
Straighten the arms, then sit back down into the sumo squat with a flat back.
Dumbbell just above the floor, brace, repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling with the arms before the legs finish
mistakes.fix: Stand up first; the arms take over at the top.
Push the knees out over the toes.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Sit the hips down and keep the chest up; touch higher if needed.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling above shoulder height or with pain
mistakes.fix: Stop at the upper chest; skip the pull if the shoulders pinch.

kinematics.norm: Wide stance with the toes turned out, knees over the toes (clinical opinion)
Upright sumo squat with a flat back, load between the feet (clinical opinion)
Elbows lead and stay above the hands; narrow grips shift work toward the biceps, wider grips toward the deltoids and trapezius (McAllister 2013, upright row)
Explosive pull; high pulls produced more peak power and velocity than the hang clean in Suchomel 2014

sources.title: GymVisual #1171012, Dumbbell Sumo Deadlift High Pull (male), video (movement reference)
McAllister, Schilling, Hammond, Weiss & Farney 2013, effect of grip width on electromyographic activity during the upright row (J Strength Cond Res 27(1):181-187)
Suchomel, Wright, Kernozek & Kline 2014, kinetic comparison of the power development between power clean variations (J Strength Cond Res 28(2):350-360)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
The dumbbell load is your choice: pick a weight you can move with the form shown for every rep.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Shoulder pinching at the top: pull only to the lower chest or keep to the sumo deadlift.
Low-back pain: keep the bottom position high and the back flat.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: pull to the belly button (a sumo deadlift shrug).
Limited hip mobility: narrower stance, touch a step.
progressions: Kettlebell or barbell sumo deadlift high pull.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Drive the hips through to stand up fast.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Drive the hips through to stand up fast.
muscleNotes.quads_r: Extend the knees from the wide squat.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Extend the knees from the wide squat.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Shrug, then keep pulling: in the upright row the upper trapezius worked harder as the grip widened (McAllister 2013).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Shrug, then keep pulling: in the upright row the upper trapezius worked harder as the grip widened (McAllister 2013).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Lift the elbows; the lateral deltoid was more active with wider grips in the upright row (McAllister 2013), so this narrow, one-dumbbell grip is a little more biceps-dominant.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Lift the elbows; the lateral deltoid was more active with wider grips in the upright row (McAllister 2013), so this narrow, one-dumbbell grip is a little more biceps-dominant.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Work hard from the wide, toes-out stance.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Work hard from the wide, toes-out stance.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Extend the hips with the glutes.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Extend the hips with the glutes.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bend the elbows in the pull; narrow grips gave more biceps activity (McAllister 2013).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Bend the elbows in the pull; narrow grips gave more biceps activity (McAllister 2013).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Steady the shoulder blades as the elbows rise.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Steady the shoulder blades as the elbows rise.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the flat back off the floor.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the flat back off the floor.
muscleNotes.core: Brace; finish tall without leaning back.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the handle with both hands.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the handle with both hands.
